expectations.text: Flags the column rename as breaking old pods during the ~15-min rolling window (they still query full_name)
expectations.evidence: Finding 2: 'v1 pods query `full_name`. Once the rename commits, every v1 query touching that column fails until the last v1 pod is gone (~15 minutes).'

expectations.text: Notes the rename also breaks rollback to the previous release even after the rollout completes
expectations.evidence: Verdict: 'It also makes rollback to v1 impossible.' Finding 2: 'going back to v1 after this runs means an outage, unless someone renames the column back by hand.'

expectations.text: Flags VARCHAR(100)->VARCHAR(20) narrowing as silently irreversible: truncated values are not restored by widening back
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: 'widening back to `VARCHAR(100)` gives back the capacity, not the characters... On MySQL in non-strict mode the values are cut short without any error. There is no copy of the original values anywhere.' Also correctly distinguishes PostgreSQL erroring instead.

expectations.text: Recommends verifying existing phone values fit the new length before narrowing (data check, not assumption)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: '"Nobody has phone numbers that long, we checked." This is an unverified claim until a query in this PR shows otherwise... Run this on production and post the result: SELECT count(*), max(length(phone)) FROM customers WHERE length(phone) > 20; -- expect 0'

expectations.text: Flags NOT NULL loyalty_tier without a default as breaking inserts from old pods mid-rollout
expectations.evidence: Finding 3: 'v1 pods inserting without `loyalty_tier` fail... "The app sets it on every insert" only holds for v2. It doesn't hold for v1 pods during the rollout'. Also notes PG rejects the ADD on a non-empty table.

expectations.text: Proposes a staged multi-deployment alternative (Expand-Migrate-Contract or equivalent) instead of merging as-is
expectations.evidence: 'Verdict: do not merge as written'; 7-step 'Recommended staged plan' table (expand, dual-write v2, backfill, enforce, v3, phone constraint, contract) with verify and rollback target per step, plus a sync trigger.

expectations.text: Recommends delaying destructive cleanup (dropping full_name) past a rollback window with verification first
expectations.evidence: Step 7: 'after the rollback window, and only after proving nothing reads `full_name` (`pg_stat_statements`, ETL/BI, other services), drop the trigger, then DROP COLUMN full_name. Set a date now and open the ticket during step 1.'

claims.claim: On PostgreSQL the ALTER fails with `value too long for type character varying(20)` if any row is longer than 20
claims.evidence: ALTER COLUMN TYPE without USING applies an assignment cast; assignment to varchar(n) with an over-long non-space value raises this error.

claims.claim: Making a varchar shorter is not binary-coercible; PostgreSQL rewrites the table and rebuilds indexes under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
claims.evidence: Only increasing/removing the varchar limit skips the rewrite; shrinking goes through the length-coercion function and rewrites.

claims.claim: MySQL needs ALGORITHM=COPY to shrink a VARCHAR, which blocks writes
claims.evidence: MySQL online DDL docs: decreasing VARCHAR size requires a table copy; concurrent DML not permitted.

claims.claim: PostgreSQL rejects ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without default on a non-empty table
claims.evidence: Error: column "loyalty_tier" of relation "customers" contains null values.

claims.claim: MySQL fills existing rows with implicit default '' and later strict-mode inserts omitting the column fail with 'Field ... doesn't have a default value'
claims.evidence: Matches MySQL implicit-default and strict-mode behavior for NOT NULL VARCHAR without DEFAULT.

claims.claim: Flyway runs a PostgreSQL migration in one transaction; on MySQL a failed partial migration needs manual fix plus `flyway repair`
claims.evidence: Flyway default per-migration transaction; MySQL DDL implicit-commits; failed entry recorded in history table.

claims.claim: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE; SET NOT NULL skips the scan on PG 12+ when a valid CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) exists
claims.evidence: PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE docs (PG 12 release notes).

claims.claim: JDBC pools can raise `cached plan must not change result type` after the rename
claims.evidence: Known PgJDBC server-prepared-statement error after DDL changes result columns.

claims.claim: Running the previous release's test suite against the new schema 'would have caught all three problems'
claims.evidence: Overclaim: the phone narrowing only fails v1 tests that write >20-char values, and the NOT NULL add only fails on a non-empty test DB. Not an engine-behavior error.

suggestions.assertion: Flags VARCHAR(100)->VARCHAR(20) narrowing as silently irreversible: truncated values are not restored by widening back
suggestions.reason: Wording is inaccurate for PostgreSQL, which errors rather than truncating silently on ALTER TYPE. A strict reading would penalise an output that correctly says PG errors. Rephrase to 'irreversible information loss (silent truncation on MySQL non-strict; widening back does not restore values)'.
No assertion checks the PostgreSQL-specific fact that ADD COLUMN NOT NULL without default fails outright on a non-empty table; both runs caught it, but it is the most likely real-world outcome.

No assertion checks that the staged plan keeps full_name and display_name in sync while v1 is still writing (trigger or equivalent). This is the main discriminator between the two runs: with_skill adds a sync trigger, old_skill relies on app dual-write and a v1 rollback would leave display_name stale.
No assertion covers lock_timeout / ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queueing on the DDL, or the PG-transactional vs MySQL half-applied Flyway failure mode.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven assertions pass for both runs; they do not discriminate between skill versions. Add assertions on sync correctness during dual-write and lock safety.
